+slug: pagerduty
+name: PagerDuty
+category: Incident management
+description: Read incidents, services and who is on call in PagerDuty, and acknowledge or resolve incidents, as you.
+enabled: true
+adapter: oauth
+auth:
+  type: oauth
+  # Each refresh returns a new refresh token. PagerDuty does not say whether
+  # the previous one stops working, so refreshes are never raced. Refresh
+  # tokens live 30 days, renewed by each refresh, for at most a year.
+  refresh: rotating
+  oauth:
+    # PagerDuty's MCP server takes OAuth but offers no dynamic registration,
+    # so each server's operator registers a Scoped OAuth app (Integrations,
+    # Developer Tools, App Registration) with the scopes below, and names its
+    # settings in PAGERDUTY_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH or saves it under Connector
+    # apps. Scoped OAuth, not Classic: Classic offers only blanket read or
+    # write, and its access tokens live 30 days, past the most Switch accepts.
+    # Scoped OAuth apps are confidential clients and must use PKCE (S256).
+    registration: static
+    client_settings: PAGERDUTY
+    # PagerDuty's documented endpoints, rather than discovery from the MCP
+    # server; the secret goes in the form body, as PagerDuty's docs send it.
+    authorization_url: https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/authorize
+    token_url: https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token
+    # Back to Core's own https callback: the server needs GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL,
+    # and nothing listens on people's computers.
+    redirect: [core]
+    # A scope the app was not registered with is not refused: PagerDuty grants
+    # a token holding only openid, and the identity call then fails. A Scoped
+    # OAuth app works at once on the account that registered it; elsewhere
+    # PagerDuty must publish it and an admin of each account install it.
+    unchecked: >-
+      Switch can't check that the app has every scope listed here, or that it
+      is installed on each PagerDuty account people connect from. Connect once
+      to confirm.
+    # PagerDuty has no endpoint to revoke one sign-in; a person revokes their
+    # own authorization on the app's page.
+    remove_access: >-
+      Revoke Switch's access in PagerDuty: open the app under Integrations,
+      OAuth Apps (Configuration, Integrations, OAuth Apps on PD Reliability
+      Platform) and revoke your user token. Until then it works until it
+      expires, within a day.
+  identity:
+    # Answers for a user's OAuth token, never an account-level one.
+    url: https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me
+    account_id: user.id
+    label: user.email
+# PagerDuty's Scoped OAuth access tokens live 1 day (documented, not
+# measured), and none can be revoked alone, so an agent's copy may outlive its
+# grant by up to that long. Agents still ask again hourly.
+token: { kind: pass_through, max_lifetime: 86400 }
+mcp:
+  servers:
+    # The US service region only. Accounts in the EU region are served at
+    # mcp.eu.pagerduty.com and api.eu.pagerduty.com, which this entry does
+    # not name. The server takes the OAuth token as Bearer.
+    - { name: pagerduty, url: "https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp" }
+access:
+  # Scopes are per resource, from PagerDuty's REST API reference for the
+  # endpoints each browse_ tool calls. users.read is needed to connect at all.
+  # A token reaches the intersection of these and the person's own role.
+  # Not asked for: event_orchestrations, status_pages and incident_workflows,
+  # whose browse_ tools are refused; and every write but incidents.write, so
+  # the manage_ tools for services, schedules, teams, event orchestrations,
+  # alert grouping and status pages are refused, as is starting a workflow.
+  # incidents.write includes creating incidents, acknowledging, resolving,
+  # reassigning and adding notes and responders.
+  read:
+    scopes:
+      - users.read
+      - incidents.read
+      - services.read
+      - schedules.read
+      - oncalls.read
+      - escalation_policies.read
+      - teams.read
+      - change_events.read
+  write:
+    scopes:
+      - users.read
+      - incidents.read
+      - incidents.write
+      - services.read
+      - schedules.read
+      - oncalls.read
+      - escalation_policies.read
+      - teams.read
+      - change_events.read
+tools: { mode: pass_through }

+---
+name: pagerduty
+description: Work with PagerDuty incidents, services, schedules and on-call through its MCP tools - see what is firing and who is on call, and acknowledge, resolve or annotate incidents when asked - acting with the owner's PagerDuty access.
+---
+
+# PagerDuty
+
+The `pagerduty` MCP server gives you PagerDuty's own tools. The `browse_`
+tools read; the `manage_` tools change things. Use them to answer what is
+firing, what it affects, who is on call and what happened during an incident.
+
+What this connection reaches:
+
+- Reading: incidents (with their alerts, notes, timeline and related or past
+  incidents), services and their alert grouping, schedules and on-call,
+  escalation policies, teams, users, change events and the activity log. You
+  see only what the owner can see in PagerDuty.
+- Changing, where the owner granted write access: incidents only - create,
+  acknowledge, resolve, reassign, and add notes or responders.
+- Not available here: status pages, incident workflows, event orchestrations
+  beyond a single service's, and changing services, schedules, teams or alert
+  grouping. Those tools are listed but PagerDuty refuses them. Say so rather
+  than trying another way.
+
+How to work with it:
+
+- Read before you change anything. Find the incident, its status, service and
+  assignees first, and quote its number, title and link so a person can check.
+- Acknowledge, resolve, reassign, escalate or create an incident only when a
+  person in the room asked for that specific change, and confirm the incident
+  number with them first. Each change notifies people and shows in PagerDuty
+  as done by the owner of this connection. Say what you changed.
+- Never resolve an incident to silence it. Resolving tells responders the
+  problem is over.
+- Prefer adding a note to changing state when you are unsure.
+- Keep queries narrow: filter incidents by status, service, urgency or a time
+  window rather than listing everything. Filtering by team or by who is
+  assigned works because you act as a person.
+- Incident details, alerts and notes can contain personal or customer
+  information. Summarise rather than pasting raw payloads into rooms, and never
+  post secrets you come across.
+
+If a tool answers that the request is not allowed or lacks a scope, the
+connection's access does not cover it: tell the person what it would take
+(write access granted to the agent, or a PagerDuty role that allows it)
+rather than trying another tool.

+PAGERDUTY = (
+    (
+        Path(__file__).parents[4]
+        / "switch_core/connections/catalog/pagerduty/connection.yaml"
+    )
+    .read_text()
+    .replace("https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth", ISSUER)
+    .replace("https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me", IDENTITY_URL)
+    .replace("https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp", MCP_URL)
+    .replace("account_id: user.id", "account_id: account.id")
+    .replace("label: user.email", "label: account.email")
+)
+PAGERDUTY_SCOPES = ["users.read", "incidents.read", "incidents.write"]
+
+
+class TestPagerDuty:
+    """PagerDuty's Scoped OAuth, as its docs describe it: the documented
+    endpoints with no discovery, PKCE with S256, scopes separated by spaces,
+    the client secret in the form body, day-long tokens, and no revocation."""
+
+    async def test_signs_in_at_its_documented_endpoints_with_pkce(self) -> None:
+        vendor = FakeOAuthServer(lifetime=86400)
+        adapter, _ = _adapter(vendor, PAGERDUTY)
+        verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
+        url = await adapter.authorization_url(
+            redirect_uri=REDIRECT,
+            state="state-1",
+            code_challenge=s256(verifier),
+            scopes=PAGERDUTY_SCOPES,
+        )
+        assert url.startswith(f"{ISSUER}/authorize?")
+        query = parse_qs(urlsplit(url).query)
+        assert query["scope"] == ["users.read incidents.read incidents.write"]
+        assert query["code_challenge_method"] == ["S256"]
+        assert query["code_challenge"] == [s256(verifier)]
+        # Nothing PagerDuty does not document, and never the secret.
+        assert "resource" not in query and "prompt" not in query
+        assert "client_secret" not in url
+        back = parse_qs(urlsplit(vendor.authorize(url)).query)
+        signed_in = await adapter.exchange_code(
+            code=back["code"][0],
+            verifier=verifier,
+            redirect_uri=REDIRECT,
+            scopes=PAGERDUTY_SCOPES,
+        )
+        [exchange] = vendor.token_requests
+        assert exchange["client_secret"] == STATIC_CLIENT_SECRET
+        assert exchange["code_verifier"] == verifier
+        assert "resource" not in exchange
+        assert signed_in.secret.expires_at == pytest.approx(time.time() + 86400, abs=5)
+        # Endpoints come from the catalog: nothing was discovered.
+        assert not any(".well-known" in path for path in vendor.paths)
+
+    async def test_a_refresh_sends_the_secret_and_keeps_the_newest_token(
+        self,
+    ) -> None:
+        vendor = FakeOAuthServer(lifetime=86400)
+        adapter, _ = _adapter(vendor, PAGERDUTY)
+        secret = await _sign_in(adapter, vendor)
+        renewed = await adapter.refresh(secret)
+        assert renewed.values["refresh_token"] != secret.values["refresh_token"]
+        assert vendor.token_requests[-1]["grant_type"] == "refresh_token"
+        assert vendor.token_requests[-1]["client_secret"] == STATIC_CLIENT_SECRET
+
+    async def test_says_where_people_revoke_it_since_switch_cannot(self) -> None:
+        vendor = FakeOAuthServer(lifetime=86400)
+        adapter, _ = _adapter(vendor, PAGERDUTY)
+        secret = await _sign_in(adapter, vendor)
+        with pytest.raises(ConnectionNotRevocable, match="OAuth Apps"):
+            await adapter.revoke_connection(secret)
+        assert vendor.revoked == []

+## PagerDuty
+
+Built from PagerDuty's documentation and REST API reference, not yet from a
+sign-in run; the operator's setup is in
+[`docs/old/pagerduty-setup.md`](../old/pagerduty-setup.md).
+
+- **Why OAuth, not a key.** PagerDuty's remote MCP server
+  (`https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp`) takes a user API key or an OAuth token.
+  A key never expires, so Switch would neither connect nor grant it (see
+  Keys); an OAuth token expires, and can be narrowed per resource. PagerDuty
+  offers no dynamic registration, so each server's operator registers a
+  **Scoped OAuth** app and saves it under Connector apps, or names it in
+  `PAGERDUTY_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH` (`registration: static`). Classic User OAuth
+  is not used: it has only blanket `read` or `write`, and its access tokens
+  live 30 days, past the week an entry may name.
+- The endpoints are PagerDuty's documented ones,
+  `https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/authorize` and `/oauth/token`, named in
+  the entry rather than discovered, so the secret goes in the form body as
+  PagerDuty's docs send it. Scoped OAuth apps are confidential clients and
+  must use PKCE with S256, which every sign-in sends. The browser comes back
+  to Core's own callback, so the server needs `GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL`.
+- Access tokens live a day and refresh tokens 30 days, for at most a year
+  of refreshes. Each refresh returns a new refresh token; PagerDuty does not
+  say whether the old one survives, so the entry treats them as rotating.
+- The MCP server takes the token as `Bearer`. The identity call is
+  `GET https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me`, which answers only for a user's
+  token, never an account-level one; the connection is named by the user's
+  email and keyed by their user id.
+- **Scopes** are per resource, taken from the REST API reference for the
+  endpoints each `browse_` tool calls. Read: `users.read` (needed to connect
+  at all), `incidents.read`, `services.read`, `schedules.read`,
+  `oncalls.read`, `escalation_policies.read`, `teams.read` and
+  `change_events.read`. Write adds `incidents.write` alone: creating,
+  acknowledging, resolving and reassigning incidents, and adding notes and
+  responders. Not asked for: event orchestrations, status pages and incident
+  workflows, and writing to services, schedules, teams and alert grouping, so
+  those tools are listed but refused. A token reaches the intersection of its
+  scopes and the person's own PagerDuty role.
+- A scope the app was not registered with is not refused: PagerDuty grants a
+  token holding only `openid`, and the identity call then fails. The app's
+  scopes must match the entry's, which the check under Connector apps cannot
+  see; it is the entry's `unchecked`.
+- A Scoped OAuth app works at once on the account that registered it. People
+  on other PagerDuty accounts can authorize it only once PagerDuty publishes it
+  and an admin of their account installs it.
+- PagerDuty has no endpoint that revokes one sign-in. A person revokes their
+  own token on the app's page under Integrations, OAuth Apps, which the
+  disconnect says; an admin can revoke every token the app holds. Until then a
+  token works until it expires, within a day.
+- The US service region only. EU accounts are served at
+  `mcp.eu.pagerduty.com` and `api.eu.pagerduty.com`, which an entry cannot
+  choose per connection today.
+
+To connect: Settings, Connections in Switch Console, then PagerDuty. To roll
+back, add `pagerduty` to `DISABLED_SERVICES`, remove its client under
+Connector apps or unset `PAGERDUTY_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH`, or set the entry's
+`enabled: false`.

+# PagerDuty on a self-hosted server
+
+Agents can read their owners' PagerDuty incidents, services, schedules and
+on-call, and, with write access, acknowledge, resolve and annotate incidents,
+once the server's operator registers a PagerDuty Scoped OAuth app. Each person
+then connects their own PagerDuty account from Switch Console and turns
+PagerDuty on for the agents they choose. How it works is in
+[`docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`](../design/service-connections-v2.md),
+under PagerDuty.
+
+Without the app, PagerDuty is listed on the server as not set up.
+
+## What you need
+
+- A **PagerDuty account** to own the app, with a Manager, Global Admin or
+  Account Owner role: App Registration is open to those alone. Use an account
+  your organization owns; an app can't be moved to another account later.
+- The server's **`GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL`**: the address people reach Switch at.
+  PagerDuty sends people back to Switch there; without it, PagerDuty cannot be
+  set up.
+- Accounts in PagerDuty's **US service region**. EU-region accounts are served
+  at other addresses, which Switch does not use yet.
+
+## Register the app
+
+In PagerDuty, open **Integrations**, **Developer Tools**, **App Registration**,
+and create a new app:
+
+1. **Name** it as people should see it when PagerDuty asks them to authorize
+   it, for example "Switch".
+2. Add **OAuth 2.0** functionality and choose **Scoped OAuth**, not Classic
+   User OAuth. Classic offers only blanket read or write, and its tokens live
+   longer than Switch accepts.
+3. **Redirect URL**: the server's callback, exactly:
+   ```
+   <GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL>/gateway/service-connections/pagerduty/flows/callback
+   ```
+   If the public URL changes, change it here too, or sign-ins fail.
+4. **Scopes**: exactly these nine.
+   - `users.read`
+   - `incidents.read`, `incidents.write`
+   - `services.read`
+   - `schedules.read`
+   - `oncalls.read`
+   - `escalation_policies.read`
+   - `teams.read`
+   - `change_events.read`
+
+   PagerDuty does not refuse a sign-in that asks for a scope the app lacks: it
+   hands out a token that holds none of them, and connecting fails. Leave out
+   every other write scope: without them PagerDuty refuses agents' attempts to
+   change services, schedules, teams, event orchestrations or status pages.
+5. **Save**, and copy the app's **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.
+
+The app works at once for people on the PagerDuty account that registered it.
+For people on other PagerDuty accounts, PagerDuty must publish the app, and an
+admin of each account install it.
+
+## Give Switch the client
+
+In Switch Console, open **Admin** in the sidebar and **Connector apps** under
+Server, or in the Switch dashboard open **Connectors** beside Users. Choose
+**Set up PagerDuty**. The dialog walks the steps above, with the redirect URL
+to copy and the scopes to choose; paste the app's **Client ID** and **Client
+Secret** and choose **Check and save**. Switch first asks PagerDuty about the
+client, and saves it only if PagerDuty accepts the client ID and secret
+together. That cannot show the app's scopes or where it is installed, so
+connect once yourself to confirm. The secret is stored encrypted and is in use
+at once.
+
+### Or, from configuration
+
+Write the app's client id and secret to a JSON file on the server, readable by
+switch-core alone and never committed anywhere:
+
+```json
+{"client_id": "<client id>", "client_secret": "<client secret>"}
+```
+
+Then point switch-core at it with an absolute path and restart it:
+
+```bash
+PAGERDUTY_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH=/etc/switch/pagerduty-client.json
+```
+
+While it is set, configuration wins over a client saved in the dashboard.
+
+## What people do
+
+1. In Switch Console: Settings, Connections, PagerDuty, Connect, choosing
+   read-only or read and write. The browser opens PagerDuty's authorization
+   page and comes back to Switch.
+2. On an agent's page, the agent's owner turns PagerDuty on. The agent acts as
+   its owner: what it acknowledges, resolves or notes shows in PagerDuty as
+   done by them, and it reaches no more than their PagerDuty role allows.
+
+PagerDuty has no way for Switch to revoke a sign-in. When someone disconnects,
+Switch forgets the token and tells them to revoke it on the app's page under
+Integrations, OAuth Apps; until then it works until it expires, within a day.
+An admin can revoke every token the app holds there, or uninstall it.
+
+## Switching it off
+
+Any of these lists PagerDuty as unavailable, with its reason, and stops
+agents' next token requests:
+
+- add it to `DISABLED_SERVICES`, e.g.
+  `DISABLED_SERVICES='{"pagerduty": "Paused while we review access."}'`;
+- remove its client under Connector apps;
+- unset `PAGERDUTY_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH`, where it is set from configuration.
